text:
alice.h: Heads up — a customer (AcmePayments) is seeing intermittent 401s for SSO-signed callbacks over the last 30m. Error in logs is `signature verification failed` but the jwks endpoint shows the matching kid present.

bob_ops: Repro steps from support: 1) request comes in from idp with header kid `k_2026_04_b` 2) our verifier tries to verify -> 401 intermittently 3) curl of https://idp.example.com/.well-known/jwks.json shows kid present.

jamie_support: Posting the exact token header they sent (redacted):
```
{"alg":"RS256","kid":"k_2026_04_b"}
```
And our verifier log snippet: `verify: kid=k_2026_04_b; jwks_cache_hit=true; signature_valid=false; reason=signature-mismatch`

carol_sre: Hmm — two hypotheses: (A) JWKS is behind a CDN/CNAME with stale cache so our fetch sees an old key for some edge nodes, (B) token actually signed with a short-lived ephemeral key not immediately present in JWKS due to propagation, or (C) subtle alg/encoding mismatch.

alice.h: Support says they only see failures for ~1-2% of callbacks and usually recover after 10-30s. Timeline aligns with IdP key rotation window. Also observed in our trace: requests that fail route through a different POP (us-west-2 edge) than successful ones.

bob_ops: Repro tried from curl across regions: sometimes verification passes, sometimes fails. When we force-fetch jwks.json immediately after a failing request it returns the new kid. Looks like caching in front of the idp endpoint.

carol_sre: Quick mitigation options: 1) In verifier, on signature failure when token header.kid present: force-refresh JWKS and retry verification once. 2) Add small clock/alg leeway in parser (we already have 5s leeway, consider 10s only if safe). 3) For long term, add exponential backoff+stale-while-revalidate for jwks fetch or use conditional GET + origin cache-control.

jamie_support: Customer-facing workaround: ask IdP to ensure JWKS endpoint sets conservative Cache-Control (e.g., max-age=5, must-revalidate) or add cache-busting query param on rotation. They can also publish rotation schedule.

alice.h: Logging hints — capture `kid` on failure and whether jwks_cache_hit=true/false. We saw `jwks_cache_hit=true` in failing logs which points to stale cache.

carol_sre: Implementation note — be careful to avoid thundering herd on refresh. If we force-refresh on signature failure, ensure singleflight across processes and short circuit if refresh in progress. Also record metric `jwks_refresh_triggered_by_sigfail`.

bob_ops: Example quick fix patch (pseudo):
```
if verify(token) == SIG_FAIL and token.kid != null {
  if try_refresh_jwks_once(token.issuer) {
    return verify(token)
  }
}
```
Make sure try_refresh_jwks_once uses a singleflight/keyed mutex.

oncall-bot: Assigned to @carol_sre for triage — ETA 2h.

carol_sre: I'll take and implement the guarded refresh + metric. Will also add a debug flag to temporarily increase jwks fetch TTL logging per customer so support can correlate.

alice.h: Thanks — can you also draft a concise note for support with exact reproduction commands? Support wants to run regionized curl and show trace IDs. Example commands: 
```
curl -v "https://idp.example.com/.well-known/jwks.json" -H "Cache-Control: no-cache"
curl -v "https://our-api.example.com/callback" -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -H "X-Request-ID: <id>"
```
Include capturing `X-Request-ID` and POP header.

jamie_support: I'll send the workaround to the customer and ask for timestamped traces + sample failing token. Also requesting IdP ops to reduce jwks TTL.

alice.h: Closing notes: root cause looks like JWKS edge/CDN staleness during rotation causing intermittent signature mismatches. Short-term: implement single-refresh-on-sigfail + support guidance. Long-term: work with platform to tighten cache-control or use conditional fetches.

jamie_support: :thumbsup: will update once customer confirms.
